q: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
exp: Mitochondria produces ATP through cellular respiration.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall cell organelles and their functions
• Nucleus: Contains DNA, controls cell activities
• Ribosome: Site of protein synthesis
• Mitochondria: Site of ATP production (cellular respiration)
• Golgi apparatus: Packages and transports proteins

Step 2: Identify the 'powerhouse'
• Mitochondria produces energy (ATP) through cellular respiration
• This is why it's called the POWERHOUSE

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Nucleus): Control center, not energy production ✗
• Option B (Ribosome): Makes proteins, not energy ✗
• Option C (Mitochondria): Produces ATP = powerhouse ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Golgi): Packages proteins ✗

The correct answer is C) Mitochondria.

q: The process by which green plants manufacture their food is:
exp: Photosynthesis is how plants make food using sunlight.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define each process
• Respiration: Breaking down glucose to release energy
• Photosynthesis: Making glucose using sunlight, CO₂, and water
• Transpiration: Loss of water vapor from leaves
• Digestion: Breaking down food (animals only)

Step 2: Recall photosynthesis equation
• 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + sunlight → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
• Carbon dioxide + Water + Light → Glucose + Oxygen

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Respiration): Energy release, not food making ✗
• Option B (Photosynthesis): Food manufacturing ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Transpiration): Water loss ✗
• Option D (Digestion): Animal process ✗

The correct answer is B) Photosynthesis.

q: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
exp: Group O negative can be given to any blood type.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall blood group compatibility
• Group A: Can donate to A and AB
• Group B: Can donate to B and AB
• Group AB: Universal RECIPIENT (can receive from all)
• Group O: Universal DONOR (can donate to all)

Step 2: Understand why O is universal donor
• Group O has no A or B antigens on red blood cells
• No antigens = no immune reaction in recipients

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A: Limited donor ✗
• Option B: Limited donor ✗
• Option C: Universal recipient ✗
• Option D: Universal donor ✓ Correct!

The correct answer is D) Group O.

q: The basic unit of inheritance in living organisms is:
exp: Genes are the basic units of heredity.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define each term
• Cell: Basic structural unit of life
• Nucleus: Contains genetic material
• Gene: Segment of DNA that codes for a trait
• Chromosome: Structure containing many genes

Step 2: Understand the hierarchy
• Cell → Nucleus → Chromosome → GENE (unit of inheritance)

Step 3: Identify the unit of inheritance
• Genes determine traits passed from parents to offspring

Step 4: Analyze options
• Option A (Cell): Structural unit ✗
• Option B (Nucleus): Contains DNA ✗
• Option C (Gene): Unit of inheritance ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Chromosome): Carries genes ✗

The correct answer is C) Gene.

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the liver?
exp: Insulin is produced by the pancreas, not the liver.
ai_exp:

Step 1: List liver functions
• Bile production ✓
• Detoxification of harmful substances ✓
• Glycogen storage ✓
• Protein synthesis ✓
• Breakdown of old red blood cells ✓

Step 2: Identify pancreas functions
• Insulin production ✓
• Glucagon production ✓
• Digestive enzyme production ✓

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Bile): Liver function ✗ (This IS a liver function)
• Option B (Detoxification): Liver function ✗
• Option C (Insulin): PANCREAS function ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Glycogen): Liver function ✗

The correct answer is C) Insulin production.

q: The process by which water moves from root hairs to the xylem is called:
exp: Osmosis is water movement through a semi-permeable membrane.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define each process
• Diffusion: Movement of molecules from high to low concentration
• Osmosis: Movement of WATER through semi-permeable membrane
• Transpiration: Water LOSS from leaf surfaces
• Active transport: Movement against concentration gradient (needs energy)

Step 2: Identify the specific process
• Water from soil → root hairs → xylem
• This is water movement through cell membranes = OSMOSIS

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Diffusion): General molecules, not specific to water ✗
• Option B (Osmosis): Water movement ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Transpiration): Water loss from leaves ✗
• Option D (Active transport): Needs energy ✗

The correct answer is B) Osmosis.

q: Which vitamin is produced by the skin when exposed to sunlight?
exp: Vitamin D is synthesized in skin upon UV exposure.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall vitamin sources
• Vitamin A: Carrots, liver, dairy
• Vitamin C: Citrus fruits, vegetables
• Vitamin D: SKIN (via sunlight), fish, eggs
• Vitamin K: Gut bacteria, leafy greens

Step 2: Identify sunlight-produced vitamin
• UV rays trigger Vitamin D synthesis in skin
• Called the 'sunshine vitamin'

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A: Dietary only ✗
• Option B: Dietary only ✗
• Option C: Sunlight synthesis ✓ Correct!
• Option D: Bacterial synthesis ✗

The correct answer is C) Vitamin D.

q: The number of chromosomes in a normal human body cell is:
exp: Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs) in body cells.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall human chromosome numbers
• Body cells (somatic): 46 chromosomes (23 pairs)
• Gametes (sperm/egg): 23 chromosomes (haploid)
• Autosomes: 44 (22 pairs)
• Sex chromosomes: 2 (XX or XY)

Step 2: Identify what's asked
• Normal BODY cell = 46 chromosomes

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (23): Gamete number ✗
• Option B (44): Autosome count only ✗
• Option C (46): Body cell total ✓ Correct!
• Option D (48): Incorrect (chimpanzee has 48) ✗

The correct answer is C) 46.

q: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
exp: The cerebellum controls balance and coordination.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall brain parts and functions
• Cerebrum: Thinking, memory, voluntary movement, senses
• Cerebellum: BALANCE, posture, coordination
• Medulla oblongata: Heart rate, breathing, blood pressure
• Hypothalamus: Temperature, hunger, thirst, sleep

Step 2: Match the function
• Balance + Coordination = Cerebellum

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A: Higher brain functions ✗
• Option B: Balance/coordination ✓ Correct!
• Option C: Autonomic functions ✗
• Option D: Homeostasis ✗

The correct answer is B) Cerebellum.

q: The process of cell division that produces gametes is:
exp: Meiosis produces gametes with half the chromosome number.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define cell division types
• Mitosis: Produces 2 identical diploid cells (growth/repair)
• Meiosis: Produces 4 haploid cells (gametes)
• Binary fission: Asexual reproduction in bacteria
• Budding: Asexual reproduction in yeast

Step 2: Recall meiosis characteristics
• Reduces chromosome number by HALF
• Produces sperm and egg cells
• Creates genetic variation

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Mitosis): Growth/repair ✗
• Option B (Meiosis): Gamete production ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Binary fission): Bacterial ✗
• Option D (Budding): Yeast ✗

The correct answer is B) Meiosis.
